name: Polycab India Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest wires and cables maker (house wires, power and control cables, special cables, EPC for rural electrification) with a growing FMEG business (fans, lights, switches, switchgear, pumps, solar inverters). 61.4% promoter-held, nearly debt-free but with rising working-capital loans. Revenue Rs 34,609 cr TTM (+41%), OPM 14%, profit Rs 3,202 cr. Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026): record sales Rs 9,899 cr (+53%), PAT ~Rs 990 cr (+43%). 'Project Spring' targets W&C EBITDA 11-13% and FMEG 8-10% by FY30 with growth ~1.5x industry. EHV cable plant is due FY28. Segment shares are model estimates.

exposures.mechanism: Copper is ~55% of W&C cost; pricing is metal-linked with near-daily list revisions. +10% copper -> revenue +~5.5% with absolute EBITDA broadly unchanged (margin % falls) but 2-4 weeks of unhedged inventory yields a transient gain (+0.2% revenue ≈ +1.4% EBITDA at 14% OPM) and boosts reported growth (Q2 revenue +53% vs volume growth high/mid single digits). Demand elasticity and working capital (interest cost up Rs 94 cr/qtr) are offsets. Net +1 after persistence 0.25; range includes negative for destocking. Pack +1.36 (t=+1.3) agrees in sign.

evidence.source: CNBC TV18 / NDTV Profit / Saur Energy
evidence.note: Q2 FY27 revenue +53%, PAT +43% (Rs 977-990 cr); W&C revenue Rs 8,301 cr +47.4% helped by metal prices

exposures.mechanism: Aluminium conductors ~8% of costs; pass-through similar to copper; small net inventory gain. Pack +1.44 (t=1.2). Aluminium is -19.6% since June.
PVC/XLPE/FRLS compounds ~8% of costs; +10% -> costs +0.8% -> EBITDA -5.7% at 14% OPM; ~70% recovered with lag; persistence 0.25 -> -0.4.

Government and utility projects (RDSS, BharatNet, metro, transmission); order book ~Rs 9,000-10,000 cr in BharatNet/RDSS (search summary). +10% capex growth -> W&C volumes +3% -> EBITDA +4% (OPM 14%) -> persistence 0.7 -> ~+3.5.
Industrial and infra wires (LT/HT power, special cables); +10% capex -> volumes +3% -> EBITDA +4%; persistence 0.7 -> ~+3.5.
Housing wire (~35% of W&C volumes, model estimate) and FMEG (fans, lights, switches) demand; +10% housing volume -> W&C +3.5%, FMEG +6% -> EBITDA +5% -> persistence 0.6 -> ~+3.
EHV/HV cables (new EHV plant targeted FY28) and transmission buildout; +1 unit = +15% HV/EHV demand -> higher-margin mix -> ~+4.
Data-centre power and structured cabling, special cables; ~3% of demand -> +1 unit doubles growth there -> ~+2.5 with sentiment.
Solar/wind cables and inverters; stronger support -> +5% W&C demand from renewable EPC.
FMEG (fans, switches, lights, appliances) ~8% of sales; +5 pp urban demand -> FMEG +8% -> +1.
Moderate debt (interest Rs 94 cr/qtr, rising) and working-capital loans; P/E 37.5. +25 bp -> funding cost +0.5% of EBITDA and de-rating -> ~-1.5.
Exports ~8% of sales; copper cathode priced in USD but passed through; net ~neutral, small export benefit.

New entrants (Jefferies note 2026-10-16: 'Polycab vs new competition') and capacity additions by KEI, Havells, Finolex, Adani/Birla-type players threaten the 14% OPM. +1 unit = 100 bp W&C margin erosion sustained -> EBITDA -6.5% at 14% OPM; structural persistence but ~60% probability weight -> ~-6.
PLI for electrical and IT hardware supports FMEG; small.
